name: Hyperconsciousness
description: Developer-alpha Rust knowledge store with encrypted, signed, append-only records, device sync, and scoped, expiring access for agents through MCP.
tagline: Encrypted knowledge with scoped agent access
approachDetail: Signed author logs and encrypted blobs are authoritative; bounded in-memory snapshots and a rebuildable encrypted search index support retrieval.
searchDetail: Case-insensitive substring matching with kind, tag, date and grant filters; no embedding or semantic search backend.
storageDetail: Encrypted append-only author logs, blob manifests and rebuildable encrypted indexes; optional replication and remote ciphertext storage.
mcpDetail: Stdio MCP via hc mcp --as <grant-id>; exposes search, recent, record, remember and remember_many, with read/write permissions checked separately.
toolSupportDetail: Configure the locally built hc executable and an existing store/grant. Company gateway mode additionally requires client-side request signing.
scopesDetail: Separate stores and independently encrypted spaces; grants constrain record kinds, tags, sensitivity, time and allowed actions. These are server access controls, not OS process isolation.
duplicateDetail: Explicit managed captures use principal-bound source identity and version for retry idempotency and conflicting-retry detection. Legacy writes can duplicate; no general semantic deduplication.
retentionDetail: Append-only history persists; managed text captures support logical correction/retraction. Grant expiry does not erase history or copies already received. This is not a backup durability guarantee.
multiUserDetail: Owner-signed company member/group policy and device proofs gate existing grants on every call; requires enrollment and request signing, with no bundled hosted team portal.
crossMachineDetail: Signed encrypted history replicates across configured devices using sync adapters; a local write receipt does not prove replication.
webUiDetail: Optional separately installed HC Atlas local read-only dashboard for metadata and authenticated record browsing; requires an existing HC installation.
tokenBudgetingDetail: Search/recent have result limits, excerpt limits and serialized response character budgets; record expands an individual reference. No tokenizer-based max_tokens guarantee.
contextInjectionDetail: The agent calls MCP retrieval tools. Context-window assembly, automatic skill activation and orchestration belong to the external harness.
networkDetail: Local storage, CLI and stdio MCP can operate without a hosted service after installation; remote sync and remote readers require their configured network route.
auditTrailDetail: Signed append-only history and grant-scoped read receipts can be inspected with hc audit; ordinary hc read does not perform a full integrity check.
pros: Encrypted local storage with signed append-only history
Scoped, expiring and revocable agent grants
Device replication without a required hosted service
Bounded retrieval with durable record references and read receipts
cons: Developer alpha requiring a Rust source build and manual store/grant configuration
Keyword retrieval without semantic search; legacy writes have no retry deduplication
No independent security audit; grants do not sandbox owner-account processes or hide returned plaintext from hosted models
notes: Evaluated from public source revision d2152ce2154affccc47f35a34876b066740d52ad. The public repository excludes private Companion, phone apps and private agent orchestration. No live deployment or performance benchmark was run for this comparison.
